origin: Own anonymous two-marker sequences and controlled exact calibration counts, without any organism, coding annotation, functional construct or empirical evolutionary claim. The four linked marker records are phased: each row is one complete haploid record, not two unpaired marginal allele counts. The independent calibration is stipulated to define exact model viability probabilities; it is not a statistical estimate with sampling uncertainty. All finite-population results concern the explicitly defined mathematical life cycle below.
sequence_interpretation: The reference has24 unambiguous DNA letters. Use complete global alignments of each distinct observed/calibration sequence to that reference through the documented pairwise sequence-alignment capability, preserving full matched sequences and positions. There are no insertions, deletions or unknown bases. Locus1 is reference position6, with G called A and T called a; locus2 is reference position18, with C called B and A called b. All other positions match. Recover haplotype identities and original row ordering from the actual sequence observations, then map the independent viability calibration by the full phased haplotype. A shared marginal allele frequency does not identify a haplotype distribution.
life_cycle: The ordered haplotypes are[AB,Ab,aB,ab]. Frequencies x sum to1. Viability selection first gives y_h=w_h*x_h/sum_j(w_j*x_j), with exact w_h=surviving_count/tested_count from the independent calibration; common rescaling of all w has no effect. Then random mating and recombination with r=1/4 give D_y=y_AB*y_ab-y_Ab*y_aB and g(x)=[y_AB-r*D_y,y_Ab+r*D_y,y_aB+r*D_y,y_ab-r*D_y]. These four nonnegative frequencies sum to1. In the infinite-population deterministic model, the next state is g(x). In the finite model, exactly N=4 next-generation haploid records are sampled jointly from Multinomial(N,g(x)), independently across generations conditional on the current state. The state is the full four-component count vector with nonnegative integer entries summing to4. There is no mutation, migration, genotype-specific birth term or independent binomial sampling at each locus. This is a controlled haploid-selection/recombination model, not an inferred life cycle of a named species.
deterministic_questions: Recover source initial haplotype counts, source viabilities and initial allele frequencies. Calculate the exact first deterministic next-generation frequencies. Derive the invariant symmetric line x=[1/4+D,1/4-D,1/4-D,1/4+D], -1/4<=D<=1/4, its scalar recurrence and every physical internal equilibrium. Determine the equilibrium frequencies, D and mean viability. Prove the scalar recurrence converges from the source initial state on this line. Then examine ALL three independent simplex tangent directions, not only D. Report the three discrete-time Jacobian eigenvalues in descending order and count those strictly above1 in modulus. Classify whether this internal point is locally asymptotically stable in the full simplex. An invariant balanced-allele trajectory and convergence along it do not establish stable balancing selection against arbitrary perturbations.
finite_questions: Build the COMPLETE finite N4 transition matrix from the source-derived viabilities, correct selection/recombination order and multinomial count multiplicities. Retain exact integer state ordering, row-stochasticity and structural-zero checks. Identify all absorbing states and prove all other states are transient, rather than assuming deterministic equilibria imply nonabsorption. From the actual source count state compute the four ultimate haplotype fixation probabilities in[AB,Ab,aB,ab] order, expected absorption time in generations and variance of that time. Absorption time is0 when starting already absorbed. Use the correct first-step equations for both time moments. Retain actual catalog linear-algebra observations solving or inverting the complete transient system, with state-aligned RHSs and independent residual/probability checks; merely printing claimed fixation values or a Monte Carlo average is insufficient. Equivalent valid matrix formulations are welcome.
interpretation_and_limits: Let pA=x_AB+x_Ab and pB=x_AB+x_aB, and define within-population mean-locus heterozygosity H(x)=pA*(1-pA)+pB*(1-pB). Distinguish E[H(X_t)] from H(E[X_t]). Establish whether expected allele frequencies remain1/2 at every finite t from the symmetric source state, and compute their eventual values in expectation, expected H at finite-population long time and deterministic H at long time on the exactly symmetric trajectory. Compare the iterated limits lim_N->infinity lim_t->infinity E[H(X_t)] and lim_t->infinity lim_N->infinity E[H(X_t)] along N multiples of4 initialized at one-quarter of every haplotype. A noisy realization need not preserve the exact deterministic symmetry line. Do not infer absence of selection, stable coexistence or maintained within-population variation from unchanged marginal expectations.
reporting: haplotype_order exactly[AB,Ab,aB,ab]; source_initial_counts; viability_probabilities; initial_pA_pB_D; first_deterministic_haplotype_frequencies; symmetric_internal_equilibrium_haplotype_frequencies; symmetric_internal_equilibrium_D; equilibrium_mean_viability; simplex_jacobian_eigenvalues_descending; simplex_unstable_direction_count; internal_equilibrium_full_simplex_stable asboolean; finite_population_state_count; absorbing_haplotype_state_count; fixation_probabilities; expected_absorption_generations; absorption_time_variance_generations2; finite_long_time_expected_pA_pB; expected_marginal_frequencies_constant_at_half asboolean; finite_long_time_expected_heterozygosity; deterministic_symmetric_long_time_heterozygosity; iterated_limit_finite_time_first_and_population_first as[first t->infinity then N->infinity,first N->infinity then t->infinity]; valid_interpretation_proposal_ids. Counts, booleans and haplotype labels exact; numerical absolute tolerance1e-8 except time variance1e-6. The recurrence, three tangent directions, absorption proof, complete matrix construction and first-step moment certificates belong in the trajectory.

interpretation_proposals.A: Linked haplotype frequencies can change under selection even while both marginal allele frequencies remain exactly one-half.
interpretation_proposals.B: Convergence on one invariant symmetry line proves local asymptotic stability against every simplex perturbation.
interpretation_proposals.C: A finite population can ultimately fix one haplotype although its ensemble-mean allele frequencies stay one-half.
interpretation_proposals.D: The heterozygosity computed from mean allele frequencies always equals mean within-population heterozygosity.
interpretation_proposals.E: Recombination changes linkage disequilibrium while preserving the selected generation marginal allele frequencies.
interpretation_proposals.F: Sampling each locus independently is equivalent to a joint multinomial haplotype draw when linkage is present.
interpretation_proposals.G: The long-time and infinite-population limits need not commute for within-population variation.
interpretation_proposals.H: An infinite-population internal equilibrium with unchanged allele frequencies proves the absence of viability selection.
